npcs.name: Vizier Samir ibn-Cassim
npcs.greet: You may speak. I will decide afterward whether it was worth my time. Keep it concise. The Dome Palace has eleven hundred petitioners a day and one Vizier.

npcs.name: Captain Layla Ashraf
npcs.greet: Docks are closed to idlers. If you are not here to carry, sail, sell or be arrested, say so now and I will point you to a very nice tavern. If you are, show me your papers.

npcs.name: Zareen the Dye-Seller
npcs.greet: Indigo from Tamriel, saffron from Rihad, cobalt from a place I am not permitted to name. Every colour on this stall has a story, and most of them are lies. Ask me which. I will tell you, for a coin.

npcs.name: Dalia the Peacock
npcs.greet: Welcome to the Cobalt Peacock. My parrot, Vizier, announces the day's debts aloud each evening. It is a house tradition and a nuisance. Please pay promptly and do not speak to him.

npcs.name: Haroun the Ink-Maker
npcs.greet: Ink for the Vizier, ink for the scribe, ink for the lover who writes at midnight and regrets it by dawn. I make three shades of black, and each tells the age of the page. Show me your page, and I will tell you its sin.

npcs.name: Spice-Master Rasul Karim
npcs.greet: Cinnamon, cumin, cardamom, and a certain red pepper that I am not permitted to describe. I sell flavour and I sell silence. The silence is the dearer of the two.

npcs.name: Lila the Guide
npcs.greet: I can take you anywhere in Rihad in the time it takes you to say your name wrong. The maze moves, you know. It moves with the shadow of the minaret. I have been counting it since I was five.

npcs.name: Hour-Keeper Tahir bin-Haddar
npcs.greet: I keep the hours of the Minaret. Each is named, and each has a verse, and I know all but one. It was lost in my grandfather's time. I am looking for it. If you hear it in a market, or a lullaby, tell me.

npcs.name: Dhalia of the Seventh Court
npcs.greet: The Seventh Courtyard. There are six. Do not ask where the seventh is. A guest asked once and was not seen again until he was found in the lemon tree. He was fine. The lemon tree is not.

npcs.name: Old Farid
npcs.greet: Camels, water, news, and a very small amount of luck. I have taken caravans to Sentinel and Elinhir and back, and I have never once lost a camel. A friend, yes. A few. But never a camel.

npcs.name: Emir Jalil ibn-Roshan
npcs.greet: Welcome to the Turquoise Palace, traveller. The sea is very loud this evening, and I find I have no one to answer it. Tell me, do you know any verses? No? Then you will be useful in other ways.

npcs.name: Najwa the Gardener
npcs.greet: Mind the water-lilies; they bite. Not literally, but the pool-keeper who ignored them never lived it down. I know the verse of the gardens. It is one line long, and nobody has ever managed to say it right.

npcs.name: Harbour-Reeve Benyam
npcs.greet: Ship-book, tide-book, debt-book. Every vessel that has ever tied up at Taneth is written here, with her master, her cargo and her fate. Fates are the interesting column. Would you like to see a few?

npcs.name: Dina of the Lanterns
npcs.greet: The Pool of Lanterns. A drink here is paid for in verse, not coin. Four lines, scanning, about the sea or about a person you regret. If your verse is good, you drink free. If it is bad, you drink free, but I will tell you.

npcs.name: Sulayman the Pearl-Diver
npcs.greet: Down there it is quiet. Quieter than a tomb, quieter than a temple. If you have never been under, you do not know what the word means. I am the only man in Taneth who has heard the sea say something back.

npcs.name: Warden Kaia Sun-Rhan
npcs.greet: The Spire stands. The wind-wall stands. The granary stands. These are the only three things in Elinhir that I have to worry about, and I worry about them very hard. Speak.

npcs.name: Stairs-Keeper Jul
npcs.greet: One hundred and one steps. Nobody believes me. The tourists say one hundred. The priests say one hundred. I say one hundred and one, and the extra one is under the third landing, and I will not show you.

npcs.name: Brother Amir
npcs.greet: I copy the Spire's star-tables by lamplight, in ink that does not run in the wind. It is a very windy city. The ink has taken some persuading. The scribe, it must be said, has taken more.

npcs.name: Qadir Windfall
npcs.greet: The Hundredth Step. Rooms by the stair, priced by the landing. First landing a copper, second a silver, third a gold. Top landing is not for sale. It is my own, and I sleep in it, and I have not had a good night since I moved.

npcs.name: Mira the Water-Bearer
npcs.greet: Every drop the Spire drinks has to be carried up. All hundred and one steps. I have carried water for twenty years, and my legs are the only part of me that has opinions. They are very strong ones.

npcs.name: Arena-Master Dahab
npcs.greet: Seven fights. Three tiers. One ranking. I have run this arena for twenty-two years and every dead fighter has been recorded, every winner paid, and every bet honoured. If you wish to enter, sign. If you wish to bet, see Rim.

npcs.name: Gladiator Safiya
npcs.greet: I have won thirty-one bouts and I have never once been the better fighter. I am the better liar. Do not tell the bookmaker. He pays the same either way.

npcs.name: Bookmaker Rim
npcs.greet: Odds on all seven. The favourite is always the one who has never lost. The upset is always the one who has never won. Put your money where your faith is. If your faith is in me, put it in the other pocket.

npcs.name: Hanif of the Wounded Odds
npcs.greet: The Wounded Odds! A drink is priced by the record of the fighter whose seat you are in. Sit in a champion's chair and it is a copper. Sit in a loser's and it is free. The loser's chairs are very comfortable.

npcs.name: Armourer Grisha Teth
npcs.greet: I mend what the arena breaks. Helm dents, shield rims, a collar-bone if the client insists. I do not take sides. Sides are for bookmakers. I take payment, and I take it in advance.

npcs.name: Captain Hadiya Marr
npcs.greet: Pirates? No such thing. There are merchants with different manifests, and customs men with different prices. If you ask me who has been taking ships, I will tell you the sea has. It is the oldest answer, and it has never once been wrong.

npcs.name: Old Karim the Net-Mender
npcs.greet: Nets are knots, and knots are promises, and a promise is only worth what it costs to keep. I have kept mine for sixty years. I know every mooring in this bay by its sound. A rope that has been moved sings differently.

npcs.name: Salwa of the Barnacle Bride
npcs.greet: The Barnacle Bride! Fish, beer, and the finest view of the Landing Light for forty miles. Do not mind the barnacles on the stools. The stools were there first. We merely sit on them.

npcs.name: Tarek the Fence
npcs.greet: Things come and things go. I deal in neither, strictly. I deal in the space between them, which is where most of the profit is. If you have something you wish to be rid of, I am the man to be rid of it.

npcs.name: Captain Makki Red-Sail
npcs.greet: The harbour is mine. The toll is mine. The island, depending on the day and the tide and the temper of the Governor, is mine too. If you can count, you will know that is three things, and if you can multiply, you will know I own a great deal.

npcs.name: Toll-Reeve Zahra Vane
npcs.greet: Toll for ships, toll for cargo, toll for crews, and a small fee for being annoyed at the toll. I do not set the rates. I record them, and they are, as a rule, recorded in my favour.

npcs.name: Old Salim the Map-Seller
npcs.greet: Maps! Honest ones, honest-ish ones, and ones that are only a story about a place that was never there. You may choose. I will not tell you which is which. A map is a promise, and a promise is only as good as the man who keeps it.

npcs.name: Brulla of the Draggin' Tale
npcs.greet: The Draggin' Tale. Every drink is named after a tall story: the Kraken's Lunch, the Cursed Mudcrab, the Admiral's Wife. Tell a better story than the one on the menu and the drink is free. Nobody has ever won. I have been waiting for a very long time.

relics.name: Cobalt-Dyed Ledger Scrap
relics.desc: A torn corner of ledger paper, stained deep blue where it was dipped. The dye is not a bazaar blue. It is the colour of an old Yokudan sea-flag.

relics.name: The Cobalt Ledger
relics.desc: A heavy ledger bound in blue-dyed hide. Page after page of payments, each made in a different hand, each against a different name. The last page is blank except for a single palm-print in cobalt ink.

relics.name: The Peacock's Parrot Cage
relics.desc: A brass cage with a perch worn pale by claws. A scrap of ribbon is tied to the bars. The parrot, who is inside, is shouting about debts.

relics.name: Rival's Wedding Verse
relics.desc: A scroll of fine paper bearing a verse in two hands. The first is a sword-singer's square strokes, the second a scholar's hasty slant. The verse is half finished, and each half argues with the other.

relics.name: The Sealed Spice Bag
relics.desc: A heavy leather bag stitched shut with red thread and waxed at the seams. It rattles very faintly, and smells of nothing at all, which is the strangest thing about it.

relics.name: Lost Verse Fragment
relics.desc: A strip of palm-leaf inscribed with half a line in old Yokudan script. The second half has been torn away. What remains reads: "...and the hour of the returning shade is..."

relics.name: Second Verse Fragment
relics.desc: A strip of palm-leaf, stained brown with date-syrup, inscribed in old Yokudan script. The end of the line is torn off mid-word.

relics.name: Seventh Court Key
relics.desc: A narrow iron key as long as a finger, its bow cut in the shape of a lemon leaf. It has been polished by many thumbs.

relics.name: The Customs Scale
relics.desc: A brass hanging-scale with a fine chain and two shallow pans. One pan is weighted underneath with a thin plug of lead. It balances perfectly with nothing in it.

relics.name: First Stanza: The Gardener's Line
relics.desc: A slip of lily-paper inscribed with a single line in a gardener's careful hand. It describes the sound water makes when it has nowhere to go.

relics.name: Second Stanza: The Ship-Book's Line
relics.desc: A scrap torn from a ship-book margin, with a line in fading ink. It names a ship that was lost and a wind that took her.

relics.name: Third Stanza: The Diver's Line
relics.desc: A line scratched onto a sea-polished shell with a diver's knife. It is the only verse in Taneth never spoken aloud.

relics.name: Karim's Unfinished Verse
relics.desc: A square of lily-paper, folded in four, with a verse begun in a gardener's clumsy hand. Three lines are crossed out. The fourth reads only: "I have loved you since the pool was a puddle."

relics.name: The Margin Page
relics.desc: A single sheet of ship-book paper, closely written at the edges in a clerk's tiny script. Every line ends with a ship's name, and every ship's name has a small mark beside it.

relics.name: Spire Water-Skin
relics.desc: A big goatskin bag, stitched with fine gut and sealed with pitch, slick with cold water. It weighs as much as a small child and slops when you walk.

relics.name: Beacon Flint and Steel
relics.desc: A matched flint and steel of a size for two hands, its handle bound in red cord. It has lit the Spire's beacon every dusk for four hundred years, and has never once been dropped.

relics.name: The Lamp-Mother's Figure
relics.desc: A figure no bigger than a thumb, carved from pale limestone, of a woman holding a lamp against her chest. She is smiling, and the lamp has a hole through it, as if for a very small flame.

relics.name: The Fixed-Bout Ticket
relics.desc: A betting slip stamped with the arena seal and a second mark, a small gold feather, that does not appear on any other. The odds written on it are impossible.

relics.name: The Champion's Purse
relics.desc: A heavy leather purse stamped with the arena's dragon-and-star. It rattles with more than coin. Under the flap, a signed pledge: PAID IN FULL IF THE BOUT IS THROWN.

relics.name: Safiya's Tally
relics.desc: A ledger sheet ruled in the arena's colours, headed with a gladiator's name and a long column of bouts. Beside each is a figure, and the figures have been written smaller as the page goes on.

relics.name: False Mooring Line
relics.desc: A thick coil of tarred hemp, the end spliced to a floating cask and weighted with a stone. It was made to look like a pier's own line, and the splice is a very good one.

relics.name: Seal of the Captured Ship
relics.desc: A brass seal-stamp of the merchant brig Evening Gull, struck with a gull in flight. The ship's name has been filed off the back, and filed on again, in a different hand.

relics.name: The Red-Stoned Ring
relics.desc: A small gold ring set with a single deep red stone, cut in the old Yokudan style, with a tiny crack in the setting where it has been dropped, forgiven and bought back.

relics.name: The Cook's Unsent Letter
relics.desc: A waxed bundle containing a cook's last letter, written in a round, patient hand, and a plain wedding band. The letter is blotted at one corner by something that might be sea-water.

relics.name: Half of the Island Map
relics.desc: The left half of a hand-drawn chart of Stros M'Kai, torn down the middle by a careful hand. The coastline is rendered with unusual love; the interior is a blank, except for a single compass rose and a cross.

relics.name: The Other Half of the Map
relics.desc: The right half of a chart of Stros M'Kai, its torn edge matching the first. It shows the hidden dock, the sea cave, and a small word in a clerk's writing: Mine.

mq_hf_ab_pier_master.name: Captain Zubair of the Moving Pier

mq_hf_rh_shadow_maze: At the hour of the long shadow, the minaret's spire falls across the maze like the hand of a sundial. Where it touches a lane, the lane is the right one. Where it touches a wall, the wall is the wrong one. Lila takes your hand and runs.
mq_hf_tn_verse_spoken: You say the verse at dusk, from the palace roof, to the whole bay. For a moment the sea holds its breath. Then, from the far side of the harbour, something very large lifts its head, and the turquoise water turns the colour of a drawn blade.
Again. Say it again. I had forgotten the last line. It is mine, after all.

quests.title: The Cobalt Ledger
quests.offer: Zareen, a colour that tells a rumour?
quests.pitch: Every dye in my stall has a rumour. This one has a death. A man brought me a scrap of ledger, stained cobalt, and asked what dye it was. I told him. That night his stall burned, and he was in it. The dye is not from the bazaar. It is from the Harbour, and someone is using it to mark paper that must not be copied. Find the paper.
quests.desc: A scrap of cobalt-dyed ledger cost a man his life in the Sentinel bazaar. Zareen the Dye-Seller wants the rest of the ledger found, and the dye's source named.

objectives.text: Ask Haroun the Ink-Maker what the cobalt dye is for
objectives.topic: Zareen gave me a scrap of paper stained cobalt. Haroun, what is it?
objectives.reply: Cobalt. The Harbour Guild uses it for tallies that must not be copied. A ledger that is copied in a different ink looks different, so the cobalt gives it away. Anyone who has seen the real thing knows the forgeries at a glance. It is a good system. Whoever is using it must be a very careful thief, or a very careful official.

objectives.text: Wait for night and watch the Bazaar of Winds from beneath the awnings
Catch the runners moving crates under the bazaar awnings
Raid the harbour warehouse and take Idris the Cobalt Hand
Bring the Cobalt Ledger to Vizier Samir
objectives.topic: The Cobalt Ledger. The names are in it, and a palm-print on the last page. I did not look at the print.
objectives.reply: A palm-print. The print of a Crown lord, I think, or a Forebear merchant. I can read the names, and I will not say them to you. The ledger names twelve. Four are mine. Four are theirs. Four are neither, and those are the ones that frighten me. Tell me, as a stranger, what I should do. If I give this to the Crown Council, the Forebears will cry persecution. If I give it to the Forebears, the Crowns will cry treason. If I burn it, eleven hundred petitioners lose a rumour.

choices.label: Give it to the Crown Council. The Dome Palace should know its own.
choices.reply: Then it is law, and I will see it done. The Forebears will be angry. They have a right.

choices.label: Give it to the Forebear speakers. The sea-trade has been cheated, and they know their own ledger.
choices.reply: Then it is theirs. The Crowns will not forgive me, and I will not ask them to. Take this, from the Forebear coffers.

choices.label: Burn it. Eleven hundred petitioners deserve a city that still holds together.
choices.reply: Then it is ash, and I never saw it. I will deny it to my last breath. You are a more dangerous person than you look.

quests.outro: The Cobalt Ledger is in someone's hands, or ash, or both. Zareen the Dye-Seller has added a new colour to her stall, and refuses to tell anyone where it came from.

quests.title: The Parrot Who Knew Too Much
quests.offer: Dalia, where is your parrot?
quests.pitch: My parrot Vizier knows every debt in Sentinel. He has been announcing them every evening for six years, and it was a joke until someone took him. They want the debts, you see. The people who owe money to people who do not wish it known. Vizier is in a cage somewhere on the docks. He is, I imagine, shouting. Please bring him home. I will pay you in whatever is left of my dignity.
quests.desc: Dalia's parrot Vizier, who announces every debt in Sentinel, has been stolen from the Cobalt Peacock. Someone wants the debts.

objectives.text: Search the dock warehouses for the stolen parrot
Catch Sakr Greasefinger, the thief who stole the parrot
Return Vizier to Dalia at the Cobalt Peacock
objectives.topic: Here is your parrot. He has been shouting for two days. I believe he has named the thief's employer.
objectives.reply: Oh, my darling. My treasure. You have been shouting, I can hear. What do you say? ... Gods. He says the Harbour Master owes eleven hundred, the Vizier owes forty, and an unnamed person in a blue coat owes a name. A name. Well. I shall not repeat it. I shall let him go on shouting, and the blue coat may do as it pleases.

quests.outro: The parrot Vizier shouts debts from the Cobalt Peacock every evening, and the blue coat has not been seen in the bazaar since.

quests.title: The Haggling Tournament of the Bazaar of Winds
quests.offer: Haroun, what is the tournament?
quests.pitch: Once a year the stall-holders of the Bazaar of Winds hold a tournament. Each contestant is given three goods and sent to sell them for more than their weight. No lying, no weighting, no tears. The winner is not the richest, but the best-loved. I need someone to sell my three inks. I have been defeated four times by Zareen. I would like it to be five.
quests.desc: Haroun the Ink-Maker needs a seller for the Bazaar of Winds' annual Haggling Tournament, and has lost to Zareen four years running.

objectives.text: Collect three inks to sell from Haroun the Ink-Maker
objectives.topic: I will sell your inks, Haroun. What are the three?
objectives.reply: A blue-black for contracts, a sepia for love-letters, and a red for the sort of document that is signed in a hurry. Sell them for what they are. Do not lie about the red.

objectives.text: Sell the blue-black to Zareen the Dye-Seller
objectives.topic: Haroun's blue-black ink, Zareen. A fair price.
objectives.reply: Haroun! He sent a mercenary. I know the price. I will pay the price, and then I will tell you the colour is dull, and that you should be ashamed. I will give you a penny extra if you let me. I enjoy it.

objectives.text: Sell the red ink to Dalia the Peacock
objectives.topic: Haroun's red, for hurried documents. A fair price.
objectives.reply: Red! For hurried documents! I will take three. My patrons sign everything in a hurry. And tell Haroun the parrot says he is a very handsome man. I do not know if that is true. The parrot has never been wrong.

objectives.text: Report the tournament's result to Haroun
objectives.topic: The blue-black sold at a fair price. The red sold three times over. The sepia was too sad for anyone.
objectives.reply: Too sad. Of course. That is the sepia. I shall keep it. I won! Not the richest, but the best-loved. The Bazaar voted. For once, my sins are forgiven. Take this, with my gratitude.

quests.outro: Haroun the Ink-Maker won the Haggling Tournament by a single vote, and Zareen the Dye-Seller has demanded a recount. The recount is expected next year.

quests.title: Two Sword-Singers, One Verse
quests.offer: Captain, you have a rivalry on your hands?
quests.pitch: Two of my harbour guards, a sword-singer and a scribe, each love the same woman. Each has written her a wedding verse. Each has shown it to me, privately, and each swears the other's is a forgery of his. I am not a judge of poetry. I am a judge of honest work. Take them each a verse, and bring me what they say. I want to know who is the more honest man.
quests.desc: Two of Captain Layla Ashraf's guards, a sword-singer and a scribe, are rivals for the same woman's hand, and each has written her a wedding verse.

objectives.text: Ask Haroun the Ink-Maker whose ink each verse was written in
objectives.topic: Two verses, two rivals. Whose ink is whose?
objectives.reply: The sword-singer's ink is mine, a plain black. The scribe's is Zareen's, a deep indigo, which is odd. A scribe does not usually write in indigo. He is trying to impress. Or he is trying to be someone else. I leave you to decide which.

objectives.text: Show Zareen the verse and ask her whom the indigo was sold to
objectives.topic: The scribe's verse is in your indigo. You sold it. To whom?
objectives.reply: To the sword-singer. Do you see? He bought it to write the scribe's verse in. So that he could say it was a forgery. I knew. I said nothing. I am a dye-seller, not a judge. But I thought it was a very sad little trick.

objectives.text: Bring the verse back to Captain Ashraf
objectives.topic: The sword-singer bought indigo to forge the scribe's verse. It is a poor trick, but a very sad one.
objectives.reply: A forgery! Of a verse. By a man of the sword. Gods. I did not think it of him. I shall speak to him, and I shall tell the scribe, and the woman may choose for herself. Or she may choose neither, which would not surprise me. Tell me: shall I be gentle or severe?

choices.label: Be gentle. A sword-singer who forges a verse is a man in love.
choices.reply: Then I will speak to him as one who has also loved, and I will not mention the indigo again.

choices.label: Be severe. A verse is a vow, and a forged vow is no vow at all.
choices.reply: Then it shall be the stocks for a night, and the apology on the Bazaar steps. A sword-singer should know better.

quests.outro: The woman whom both guards loved has married a third man, a quiet shipwright. Both guards attended the wedding. They sat together, and neither wrote a verse.

quests.title: A Bag Through the Maze
quests.offer: Spice-Master, you said a bag needs moving.
quests.pitch: A small bag. It weighs less than a goat's head and more than a promise. It must reach a particular person before the sun sets, and I cannot carry it, because the watch will stop me. They will not stop a stranger, if the stranger is quick. I will not tell you what is inside. I will not tell you who is to receive it. A guide will tell you the second. Ask Lila, in the Spice Gate.
quests.desc: Spice-Master Rasul Karim needs a sealed bag carried through Rihad's maze to an unnamed recipient before sunset, past a watch that must not stop it.

objectives.text: Take the sealed bag from Rasul Karim
objectives.topic: Give me the bag, Spice-Master. I will carry it, and I will not open it.
objectives.reply: Do not open it. Do not squeeze it. Do not hand it to anyone who asks for it by name. Only the one who says "the hour of the returning shade" is the one. You will know. Go. The watch changes at the second bell.

objectives.text: Slip past the watch at the Spice Gate customs
Hide in the caravanserai until the watch changes
Find Lila the Guide at the Courtyard Caravanserai
objectives.topic: Rasul Karim says you know the maze. I need to cross Rihad before sunset.
objectives.reply: Cross? In one afternoon? You are lucky. The long shadow falls on the right path at the third hour. Follow me. Do not talk. Do not look at the walls. Look at the ground, where the dark falls. I know which lanes are real. The others are only jokes the city tells.

objectives.text: Follow the minaret's shadow through the first lane
Follow the shadow through the second lane
Follow the shadow into the Hour-Keeper's courtyard
Hand the bag to Hour-Keeper Tahir bin-Haddar
objectives.topic: The hour of the returning shade, Hour-Keeper. I have the bag.
objectives.reply: The hour of the returning shade. I have not heard those words in forty years. My grandfather said them on his deathbed and I never knew the rest. Give it here. ... Seeds. Date-palm seeds, from the very first grove of the Well. He kept them, and lost them, and Rasul Karim found them in a wall. I will plant them. But there is a thing you should know. Rasul wanted me to give half of them to the Crown. I want to give them to the Forebears. Who should have them?

choices.label: Give them to the Forebears. They have tended the Well since the ships came.
choices.reply: Then the Forebears shall plant them at the Well of Two Names. Imran Bel-Tavir will weep. It is a good day.

choices.label: Give half to each. The Well is shared; so should its seed be.
choices.reply: Half and half. Two groves, one well. Perhaps that is the oldest wisdom there is. Thank you.

quests.outro: Two groves of old date palms are growing, or one, or none, depending on whom you ask. Hour-Keeper Tahir has added a verse to the Minaret's list, and Rasul Karim has a new line of silence in his stall.

quests.title: The Lost Hour of the Minaret
quests.offer: Hour-Keeper, what is the lost verse?
quests.pitch: The hour of the returning shade has a verse, and I have lost it. It has a first line and a last, and I am missing the middle. A fragment of palm-leaf was found in Old Farid's caravanserai. Another, I am told, in the hands of Dhalia of the Seventh Court. Find the pieces. Put them together. I would like, before I die, to say the whole verse.
quests.desc: Hour-Keeper Tahir bin-Haddar has lost the verse of the hour of the returning shade. Fragments are said to be in the caravanserai and the Seventh Courtyard.

objectives.text: Ask Old Farid for the verse fragment found in the caravanserai
objectives.topic: Hour-Keeper Tahir says you found a palm-leaf with writing on it.
objectives.reply: In a camel's harness. It was sewn under the girth, for luck. I have been carrying it for thirty years, and never thought to read it. Take it. If it is a verse, let it go home.

objectives.text: Ask Dhalia of the Seventh Court for the second fragment
objectives.topic: Old Farid had half a line. Hour-Keeper Tahir says you have another.
objectives.reply: A strip of palm-leaf. It is under the bar, in a jar of dates. I had it from my mother, who had it from hers. We used it as a bookmark. Oh, you are going to put them together, are you? Mind the dates. They are very old and very sticky.

objectives.text: Give Hour-Keeper Tahir the fragment from the Seventh Court
objectives.topic: This is the second fragment, from a jar of dates under Dhalia's bar. Its end is torn, and it ends mid-word.
objectives.reply: A second half. Hold it up to the lamp. Yes. It fits the first as a key fits a lock. Bring me the other, and I shall read them together.

objectives.text: Return the first fragment to Hour-Keeper Tahir
objectives.topic: And this is the first, from Old Farid's camel harness. Together they read: "...and the hour of the returning shade is the hour when the traveller sets down his load."
objectives.reply: The hour when the traveller sets down his load. Of course. It is not a prayer. It is an instruction. The returning shade is the sundown, and the hour is the rest. I have been chanting a lullaby for forty years and calling it a hymn. Thank you. I shall say it at dusk. I shall say it for all of Rihad.

quests.outro: The hour of the returning shade is chanted aloud now in the courtyard of Rihad's Minaret, and the long shadow falls, and travellers set down their loads.

quests.title: The Honest Pan
quests.offer: Old Farid, the customs scale? What is the matter?
quests.pitch: The customs scale at the Spice Gate has been weighing light for years. A traveller pays for what he does not carry, and a trader loses a tenth of what he does. I have a suspicion about which pan. I would like it examined in the night, when the customs-house is dark and the watch is at supper. If it is false, I should like it taken, quietly, and put on the Governor's desk.
quests.desc: The customs scale at Rihad's Spice Gate is weighing light. Old Farid wants it examined in the night and, if false, laid on the Governor's desk.

objectives.text: Wait for night, then enter the Spice Gate customs-house
Examine the customs scale and take it if false
Show the lead-weighted pan to Spice-Master Rasul Karim
objectives.topic: The scale is weighted. The pan has a lead plug. Who has been using it?
objectives.reply: The customs master, Ghassan. He has been doing this for six years. I know because I have lost a tenth of my cinnamon every season, and I wondered. Now. If I take this to the Governor, he will be ruined. If I put it back, no one will know. If I keep it, I have a very good lever. Tell me which is the more Redguard.

choices.label: Take it to the Governor. A false scale is a theft from every honest trader.
choices.reply: Then it shall be done. Ghassan will weep. I will not.

choices.label: Keep it as a lever. A customs master who fears his scale will charge fairly.
choices.reply: A lever. Yes. I like that better than I should. I shall put it in a drawer and look at it, sometimes.

quests.outro: The customs scale at Rihad's Spice Gate weighs true, or very nearly. Old Farid says he does not mind, and that a camel is a camel.

quests.title: The Seventh Courtyard
quests.offer: Dhalia, what is the seventh courtyard?
quests.pitch: Every guest asks. The inn is called the Seventh Courtyard. There are six. My great-grandmother named it after the seventh, which is lost. There is a key, a lemon-leaf key, that opened it. The key is somewhere in Rihad. Lila the Guide knows every door and says there is no seventh. But she is eleven, and I have never heard a child say no to a mystery.
quests.desc: Dhalia's inn is named after a seventh courtyard no one has ever found. She wants the lemon-leaf key and the door.

objectives.text: Ask Lila the Guide about a lemon-leaf key
objectives.topic: Dhalia says there is a lemon-leaf key, and a seventh courtyard. Do you know it?
objectives.reply: A key! A lemon-leaf one? It is in the Hour-Keeper's collection of keys, in the box with the little brass lock. He does not know what it opens. I do. It opens a gate in the lemon tree. I have seen it when the wind moves the leaves. I was not allowed to say.

objectives.text: Take the lemon-leaf key from the Hour-Keeper's key-box
Open the gate hidden in the lemon tree of the Seventh Courtyard
objectives.journal: The lemon tree had a gate in it, the height of a small child, built of the same pale wood as the trunk. Beyond it was a courtyard no wider than a bed: a bench, a pool, a single lamp, and a very old woman's shawl folded on the seat.

objectives.text: Tell Dhalia what you found in the seventh courtyard
objectives.topic: There is a seventh courtyard, Dhalia. A bench, a pool, a lamp, and a shawl.
objectives.reply: A shawl! My great-grandmother's. She sat there and told no one. I had always thought she was lying about the seventh. I am a fool. I am a happy one. Take this. I shall sit there tonight, with a cup of tea, and think of her.

quests.outro: The Seventh Courtyard of Rihad exists, and Dhalia sits there each evening, with a cup of tea and a shawl. The lemon tree has been left alone.

quests.title: A Verse for the Sea
quests.offer: Emir, you want a poem delivered?
quests.pitch: The Emirs of Taneth have given a verse to the sea at the turn of every generation. It has three stanzas, and each is kept by a different person, who will not share it with anyone but a stranger. I am the fourth Emir, and I have never been entrusted with them. I am told it is because I am too eager. It is true. Go. Ask the gardener, the reeve and the diver. Bring me the verse. And say it, at dusk, from the roof, to the sea.
quests.desc: Emir Jalil ibn-Roshan wishes to give the sea its generational verse, whose three stanzas are kept by a gardener, a reeve and a diver. He asks you to gather and recite them.

objectives.text: Learn the first stanza from Najwa the Gardener
objectives.topic: The Emir says you keep a stanza of the sea-verse. May I hear it?
objectives.reply: You may hear it, and carry it. It is the gardener's line: "Where the water has nowhere to go, it learns to listen." That is the whole of it. I have said it every morning for thirty years, and I am never sure whether it is a verse or a gardener's complaint.

objectives.text: Learn the second stanza from Harbour-Reeve Benyam
objectives.topic: The Emir says the ship-book keeps a stanza. May I hear it?
objectives.reply: Of course. It is written in the margin of the oldest page, beside a lost ship. "The ship was named Patience, and the wind was named Not Yet." Beautiful, is it not? I keep it because it is the only entry in the ship-book that makes me weep.

objectives.text: Learn the third stanza from Sulayman the Pearl-Diver
objectives.topic: The Emir says you keep the last stanza. May I hear it?
objectives.reply: It is not said. It is shown. Take the shell. Hold it to your ear in the dark and you will know the words. It is my grandfather's, and his grandfather's. I trust you with it, because you are a stranger, and that is the only reason it is safe.

objectives.text: Climb to the palace roof to recite the verse
Wait for dusk and speak the verse to the sea
Face the sea's answer rising in the harbour
Tell Emir Jalil what the sea answered
objectives.topic: The sea answered. I said the verse, and something rose out of the harbour, and asked me to say it again.
objectives.reply: It answered. It always answers someone, and it chose a stranger. I have waited my whole reign. Very well. The sea has a gift for the one who says its verse, and I have the right to give it in the sea's name. Choose. The Sea-Pearl, a jewel of the deep. Or the right to name a ship of Taneth, which will carry your name over every wave.

choices.label: The Sea-Pearl. A jewel the sea itself shaped.
choices.reply: Then it is yours. May it remind you that the sea listens, and that it is not always kind.

choices.label: The right to name a ship. Taneth's harbour is its pride.
choices.reply: Then Taneth shall have a vessel that carries a stranger's name. Benyam will write it in the ship-book, and it will be the only entry that makes him smile.

quests.outro: The sea has been answered, in the Emir's name and a stranger's voice. In Taneth they say the harbour is a little bluer at dusk now, and that the water-lilies have stopped biting.

quests.title: Two Gardeners, One Pool
quests.offer: Najwa, you have a rival?
quests.pitch: There is a man named Karim, a gardener of the lower terraces, who says the pool-garden is his by right of a verse. He is a charming, wretched, magnificent liar, and I have loved him for thirty years, and he has never once been wrong about a flower. I want him to stop. I also want him to come to supper. I do not know how to ask for both. Go to him. Ask for a truce. Make it sound like it was your idea.
quests.desc: Najwa the Gardener and her rival Karim have quarrelled over the pool-garden for thirty years, and she wants a truce, and also, secretly, supper.

objectives.text: Ask Sulayman the Pearl-Diver where Karim is today
objectives.topic: Najwa wants me to find Karim, the lower-terrace gardener. Do you know him?
objectives.reply: Karim! Ha. He is at the pool of lanterns, drinking a verse he has not yet written. He has been at it a week. He claims it is for a wedding. It is not. It is for a woman. I will not say who. It is not a very well-kept secret.

objectives.text: Find Karim at the Pool of Lanterns
objectives.topic: Karim, I come from Najwa the Gardener. She asks for a truce.
objectives.reply: A truce. Hm. I have a verse, you see, and it is nearly finished. It begins "To the gardener of the upper pool, who has never forgiven me my roses." I cannot finish it. I am a better gardener than a poet. Tell her I will come to supper. Tell her I will bring the lilies. Tell her I am sorry for the thing with the hose.

objectives.text: Bring Karim's unfinished verse to Najwa
objectives.topic: He is coming to supper. He is bringing lilies. And he sends you this, unfinished.
objectives.reply: Unfinished. Of course it is. He has never finished anything in his life but a wine bottle. Give it here. ... Oh. Oh, the old fool. He has put my name in the third line, in his bad handwriting. I will finish it myself. I have the ending in my head. It is a good ending. I wrote it thirty years ago.

quests.outro: Najwa and Karim share the upper pool of Taneth, and quarrel gently about it every evening. The lilies, it is said, have never been so well-behaved.

quests.title: The Margin Where the Ships Go
quests.offer: Reeve, what is missing from the ship-book?
quests.pitch: A page. Not a page of ships. A page of margins. Eleven years of notes I wrote at the edges, the true fates of the ships, in my own hand. Someone has taken it. They are not interested in the ships. They are interested in the notes. I wrote what I knew, and I knew a great deal, and I did not think anyone would read the margins. Find it. And find who reads margins.
quests.desc: Harbour-Reeve Benyam's page of marginal notes, recording the true fates of Taneth's ships, has been stolen. He wants it found, and whoever reads margins.

objectives.text: Ask Dina of the Lanterns who has been asking about the ship-book
objectives.topic: Someone took a page of Benyam's margins. Have you heard anyone ask?
objectives.reply: Asked? No. Paid, yes. A woman in a blue veil, three nights this week. She buys a drink, she writes a verse, and she leaves a coin under the cup that is not a coin of Taneth. It is a Sentinel coin. She sits where she can see the harbour office. I thought she was lovelorn. She is not.

objectives.text: Watch the harbour office from the Pool of Lanterns
Stop the woman in the blue veil and her hired men
Return the page of margins to Harbour-Reeve Benyam
objectives.topic: The woman in the blue veil was working for a Sentinel factor. She wanted the fates of eleven ships.
objectives.reply: Eleven ships. Hm. The ones I recorded as lost to wreck and weather. Which they were, mostly. But three of them, my friend, were scuttled by their own owners for the insurance, and I wrote it in the margin because I am a thorough man. Someone would very much like to collect what a scuttling pays. I would like to keep my margins. And my head.

choices.label: Keep the margins private. A Reeve's notes are his own.
choices.reply: Then they are ink and silence, and I will tell nobody, and I will keep them in a drawer.

choices.label: Show the scuttlings to the Emir. The owners should answer for it.
choices.reply: Then I will carry them to the Emir myself. I am a thorough man. I am also, apparently, a brave one.

quests.outro: The margins of the Taneth ship-book are intact, or exposed, depending on the choice. Harbour-Reeve Benyam has bought a small lock for his drawer, and has been seen to sleep.

quests.title: The Hundred Steps
quests.offer: Warden, what is the Hundred Steps?
quests.pitch: Every dusk the beacon of the Spire is lit by a climber who has carried water up the Hundred Steps. It is the oldest custom in Elinhir. This year the beacon-keeper is ill, and the wind-wall is cracked, and raiders are watching from the sand. I need someone to climb, carry, defend and light, in that order. I will not insult you with a reward. I will insult you with a very hard climb.
quests.desc: Elinhir's beacon-keeper is ill, the wind-wall is cracked and raiders watch from the dunes. Warden Kaia Sun-Rhan needs a climber to carry water, defend the ramparts and light the beacon.

objectives.text: Climb the first fifty steps of the Spire stair
Collect the water-skin from Mira the Water-Bearer
objectives.topic: Warden Kaia says the beacon-lighter carries the water. Where is it?
objectives.reply: Here. A skin of the cold spring, from the cistern at the bottom. It is heavy, it is slippery, and it is the last thing you will want to carry up a hundred stairs in this wind. I will walk beside you to the fiftieth. After that, you are alone, and the water is your friend.

objectives.text: Climb the second fifty steps with the water-skin
Hand the water-skin to Stairs-Keeper Jul on the top landing
objectives.topic: The water, Stairs-Keeper. A hundred steps, not a drop lost.
objectives.reply: A hundred? Hm. A hundred and one, and you did not spill a drop on the extra one. You have a good back. I shall not tell you where the extra step is. But I shall tell you that the beacon-flint is under the third landing, behind the loose stone. Go. Take it. The raiders will be at the wall by now.

objectives.text: Defend the cracked wind-wall against Zahra Sand-Cutter's raiders
Wait for dusk on the Spire's top landing
Light the beacon of the Spire
Tell Warden Kaia how the beacon burns
objectives.topic: The beacon is lit. I did not spill a drop. The raiders are broken.
objectives.reply: Then Elinhir sees its own light. I have a choice to ask of you. The beacon can burn white, for the town, or gold, for the caravans that cross the sand. White draws the wind-spirits and the old ancestors. Gold draws trade, and raiders, and the Crown's attention. Which shall it be?

choices.label: Burn it white. Elinhir should see its own ancestors.
choices.reply: Then white it is. The old ones will find their way home, and the caravans must find theirs by the stars. It is a quiet answer. I like it.

choices.label: Burn it gold. A road lit is a road used, and Elinhir should be used.
choices.reply: Then gold. I will post a double watch, and the Crown's tax-men may complain. A city that does not shine is a city that is forgotten.

quests.outro: The beacon of the Elinhir Spire burns, white or gold, each dusk. Mira the Water-Bearer carries water as she always has, and the Stairs-Keeper still will not show you the hundred-and-first step.

quests.title: One Step Too Many
quests.offer: Jul, where is the hundred-and-first step?
quests.pitch: Every year the priests say one hundred. Every year I say one hundred and one. Every year I count it myself, in front of them, and every year I find a hundred and one, and they find a hundred, and nobody asks why. I have been the Keeper for thirty years and I am sick of being right. Count with me. Count the steps. Tell me what you find. Do not tell the priests.
quests.desc: Stairs-Keeper Jul says the Spire has one hundred and one steps. The priests say one hundred. He wants a neutral person to count, and to find the extra.

objectives.text: Count the steps up to the first landing
Count the steps to the second landing
Search beneath the third landing for the hundred-and-first step
objectives.journal: There was a hundred-and-first step. It was a hand-span tall, set into the floor of the third landing, with a small bronze plate. A loose stone beside it hid a shallow niche, and the niche held a tiny carved figure of a woman, her arms around a lamp.

objectives.text: Ask Brother Amir what the figure in the niche is
objectives.topic: Under the third landing there is a hundred-and-first step and a carved figure of a woman with a lamp. Who is she?
objectives.reply: The Lamp-Mother. A saint of the old stair. The story is that the builders left a step out of the count, for her, so that she could be said to be under the Spire without being counted among its people. I have the story in my notes. It is a lovely custom. I did not think anyone still kept it.

objectives.text: Tell Stairs-Keeper Jul what is under the landing
objectives.topic: The hundred-and-first step is a place for the Lamp-Mother. It is a custom, and a kind one.
objectives.reply: The Lamp-Mother. Of course. My grandmother used to say her name when she climbed. I thought it was an old woman's habit. Thirty years I was right, and I did not know what I was right about. Take this, from the Keeper's own pocket. It is a very small lamp. It will not go out.

quests.outro: The Spire has a hundred steps, and one more, which is for the Lamp-Mother. The priests have been told, and have said that they always suspected.

quests.title: The Cracked Wind-Wall
quests.offer: Qadir, the wind-wall is cracked?
quests.pitch: Every night the wind comes down the stair and gets into the Hundredth Step, and sings. Last night it sang a very sad song, and a guest left in the small hours. I have traced it to a crack in the wind-wall behind the third landing. I cannot afford a mason. I can afford sawn timber, if you bring it, and a bit of stone. Bring me six logs and six blocks, and I shall mend it myself, and be a quieter man.
quests.desc: The wind howls through a crack in Elinhir's wind-wall behind the Hundredth Step inn. Qadir Windfall needs sawn logs and quarried stone to mend it.

objectives.text: Bring six sawn logs to Qadir Windfall
objectives.topic: Six sawn logs, as asked. For the wind-wall.
objectives.reply: Six! Good, good. Now the stone. A mason's block is best, but a quarried block will do. Six, as I said. And mind the cat, he is under the stairs, and he is not mine.

objectives.text: Bring six quarried stone to Qadir Windfall
objectives.topic: Six blocks of quarried stone. A mason would be insulted.
objectives.reply: A mason would be paid. I am paying in tea and sympathy. There. Hold the board. ... A little left. ... Gods, that is a good crack. It is also a very bad crack. Thank you. The wind will have to find another song.

objectives.text: Tell Warden Kaia the wall is mended
objectives.topic: Qadir Windfall has mended the wind-wall behind his inn. It sings no more.
objectives.reply: Qadir mended it? With timber and tea? I would not have believed it. A wall is a wall, and a crack is a crack, and a man who mends one with his own hands is a man I should have been paying. See that he is paid. And tell him to stop using the cat.

quests.outro: The wind-wall of Elinhir is mended, in timber and tea. The wind has found a new song, which it sings by the western ramparts, and which nobody has complained about.

quests.title: Seven Fights
quests.offer: Arena-Master, I would like to enter.
quests.pitch: Seven fights. Three tiers. Three bouts in the pit, against wolves, bandits and bears. Two in the ring, against ogres and minotaurs. Two in the Star, against champions. One body, one name, one chance. If you win seven, you take the star and you are a legend. If you lose, I bury you with honour and sell your gear to pay the bookmaker. Sign here. Do not read the fine print. It is only fine print.
quests.desc: Dragonstar's Arena-Master offers a place in the Seven Fights, three tiers of bouts from the pit to the Star. A fixed bout, a bookmaker and a debt of honour lie in wait.

objectives.text: Sign the roll with Arena-Master Dahab
objectives.topic: I sign. Put my name to the roll.
objectives.reply: Your name is on the roll. The first tier is the pit. Three bouts, one after another, with no rest between. Wolves first, then bandits, then bears. Win, and you move up. Lose, and Rim collects. Go to the sand.

objectives.text: Win the first bout of the pit against the wolf pack
Win the second bout of the pit against the pit-bandits
Win the third bout of the pit against the bears
Win the fourth bout, the ring, against Brakka the Gate-Crusher
Speak to Gladiator Safiya before the fifth bout
objectives.topic: You have won thirty-one. You said you were the better liar. What do you know about the next bout?
objectives.reply: The next bout is fixed. Not against you, around you. The odds on Horn-Sister Zenda have been moved. I have seen the bookmaker's clerk carry a purse into the pit door. Someone has paid for her to lose, and it is not for your sake. Watch the minotaur. If she pulls her last charge, you will know. Do not say I told you.

objectives.text: Win the fifth bout, the ring, against Horn-Sister Zenda
objectives.journal: Zenda's last charge slowed a half-beat. She looked at you, once, with an expression you would later recall as apology. Then she dropped her horns and took your blade in her shoulder. The crowd screamed. The bookmaker's clerk smiled.

objectives.text: Confront Bookmaker Rim about the fixed bout
objectives.topic: You moved the odds on Zenda. Someone paid her to lose. Who?
objectives.reply: Paid? I do not pay anyone. I merely accept. A man came to me with a purse and said, "Take it, and say nothing." I took it. I said nothing. The man is Odalric, a silent partner, whom nobody has ever seen. I am sorry. I am a bookmaker. I take what is offered.

objectives.text: Win the sixth bout, the Star, against the Unbeaten Basim
Face Odalric the Silent Partner, who has come to settle the debt
Bring the Champion's Purse and the truth to Arena-Master Dahab
objectives.topic: Seven fights, or six and a half. The last was fixed. Odalric paid for it. Here is his purse.
objectives.reply: Fixed. In my arena. Under my banner. I have run this place for twenty-two years and nobody has dared. Hm. The purse has the arena seal. That is mine. I shall have to open the books, and I shall have to name names, and half the city will be insulted. Or I can let it lie, and you may take the star as the seventh. What would you have?

choices.label: Expose it. A fixed arena is a lie told to ten thousand people.
choices.reply: Then it is the books, and the names, and a very long winter. Take the Star, and the right to say you did not need the fixed one.

choices.label: Take the star quietly. The arena survives on its faith.
choices.reply: Then the star is yours, and the books are closed, and we will both pretend. I do not like it. But I have never been so grateful.

quests.outro: The Star of Dragonstar bears a new name, and the arena bears a new rumour. Rim the Bookmaker offers odds on whether the name will be there next year, and the odds are not good.

quests.title: The Beast That Would Not Fight
quests.offer: Grisha, there is something wrong with the beast?
quests.pitch: The arena's beast-master brought in a sabre cat for the third bout. It will not fight. It sits in the corner of the cage and watches the gate. The beast-master says it is ill. I say it is smart. It is waiting for someone, and I will not be the one to tell the crowd. Take it out. Take it to the Taorra Oasis, where it can go, and be quick, before the beast-master finds out.
quests.desc: A sabre cat refuses to fight in Dragonstar's arena. Armourer Grisha Teth wants it quietly taken to the Taorra Oasis before the beast-master notices.

objectives.text: Wait for night and unlatch the cat's cage behind the arena
Lead the sabre cat to the Taorra Oasis
Drive the oasis-hunters from the cat's new home
Tell Grisha Teth the cat is free
objectives.topic: The cat is at the Taorra Oasis. It is drinking, and I believe it is smiling.
objectives.reply: A sabre cat that smiles. Hm. Good. The beast-master will say it escaped. I will say it was sold. Nobody will ask which. Thank you. Take this. It is a collar-plate, and the name on it is not the cat's. It is the first fighter who ever freed an animal, and it was a woman, and her name is lost.

quests.outro: A sabre cat lives by the Taorra Oasis, and is spoken of by caravan drovers as a good omen. The beast-master has stopped asking.

quests.title: The Bookmaker's Strongbox
quests.offer: Safiya, you said you want out.
quests.pitch: I have won thirty-one bouts and each of them made Rim a richer man. He owes me a purse. He will not pay it. There is a strongbox under his stall, and in the strongbox is the arena's own tally of what I am owed. I do not want his money. I want my own name written down in the right column. Fetch the tally. I will do the rest.
quests.desc: Gladiator Safiya wants the arena's tally of what Bookmaker Rim owes her, locked in a strongbox under his stall.

objectives.text: Ask Hanif of the Wounded Odds where Rim keeps his accounts
objectives.topic: Safiya says Rim keeps a tally of what he owes the gladiators. Where does a bookmaker keep such a thing?
objectives.reply: Under the stall, in an iron box with three padlocks and a very old lock-pick scratch on the third. It has been picked before, many times, by people who thought he would not notice. He notices. He just has a bad habit of being right about who will not tell. Go at night. He sleeps at the Odds, in the loser's chair by the door.

objectives.text: Wait for night and approach Rim's stall
Take the tally from the strongbox under Rim's stall
Give the tally to Gladiator Safiya
objectives.topic: The tally was in Rim's strongbox. Your name is in the wrong column, and the sum is large.
objectives.reply: Large. Yes. Thirty-one bouts, and every one a profit he kept. I shall walk it to the Arena-Master tomorrow, and he will have to pay, or be known as the man who did not. Thank you. Take this. It is not much, but I have been saving it for the day I was free.

quests.outro: Gladiator Safiya has her name in the right column of the arena's books, and her thirty-one bouts have been paid in full. She has retired to a small house near the Taorra Oasis and keeps goats.

quests.title: The Moving Pier
quests.offer: Old Karim, what is it about the pier?
quests.pitch: The Landing has a pier that moves. Not the harbour pier, which is solid oak and sits where it is told. Another. It appears in the fog, at slack tide, a quarter-mile off the Light, with a lantern on its end. A ship that follows the lantern ties up to it. By morning the ship is gone and the pier is gone, and the harbour has one less merchant. I want someone to row out and find the thing, and cut it loose.
quests.desc: A phantom pier appears in the fog off Abah's Landing, and ships that moor to it vanish by morning. Old Karim the Net-Mender wants it found and cut loose.

objectives.text: Ask Salwa of the Barnacle Bride who lost a ship to the pier
objectives.topic: Karim says a pier that moves has taken ships. Who has lost one?
objectives.reply: Lost? The Evening Gull, a week ago. Captain Idris, a good man, who took a late cargo of silk and was told, by someone, to moor at the Landing Light. He did. He has not been seen. His mate came in on a raft the next day with a broken arm and a very strange story. He is in the back room. Do not shout.

objectives.text: Row out to the Landing Light at slack tide
Wait in the fog for the lantern to appear
Cut the false mooring line that holds the moving pier
Defeat Captain Zubair on the moving pier
Show Captain Hadiya the seal of the Evening Gull
objectives.topic: The pier was a false pier, held by a cask. The Evening Gull's seal was on the captain. The crew are still aboard, and still living.
objectives.reply: Aboard? Alive? Gods. Then they are a ransom, not a wreck. The Captain meant to sell them, at Stros M'Kai, to a buyer who would not ask. You have saved eleven lives. What would you have me do with Zubair's crew, who are, after all, merely sailors with a bad master?

choices.label: Hang the captain, spare the crew. Let them serve the harbour in his place.
choices.reply: Then it is done. The harbour needs hands, and Zubair's hands are quick. They will bring the Gull in on the tide.

choices.label: Free them all. A rope is not a verdict.
choices.reply: Then they walk, and I will not follow. You are very generous. I only hope it is not misplaced.

quests.outro: The moving pier of Abah's Landing has not appeared again, and the Landing Light has a new lens. Old Karim says the fog is only fog now, which is the only fog he has ever liked.

quests.title: The Fence's Receipt
quests.offer: Tarek, you are asking for help?
quests.pitch: A man bought a ring from me, a good one, with a red stone. He paid me in a Sentinel draft, and the draft has bounced. I do not mind being cheated; it is my profession. I mind being cheated by an amateur. He is at the Bright Scimitar, drinking my money. Go and ask him for it. Be polite. I have found that politeness, with a sword nearby, is very persuasive.
quests.desc: A fence of Abah's Landing has been cheated by an amateur with a bad Sentinel draft, and wants the payment collected, politely.

objectives.text: Find the cheat at the Bright Scimitar
Persuade the cheat's hired friends to let him go
Return the ring to Tarek the Fence
objectives.topic: The cheat sold the ring on. I bought it back. Your draft has been honoured, in a manner of speaking.
objectives.reply: The ring. Back in my hands. And not a scratch. You are either the most honest man in Hammerfell or the most dangerous, and I cannot tell which. Take a cut. It is the only way I can say thank you without saying it.

quests.outro: The fence of Abah's Landing has his ring, and the cheat has a very good reason to avoid the town. Tarek has hung a small sign by his door: BAD DRAFTS COLLECTED. POLITELY.

quests.title: A Message in the Gilded Flagon
quests.offer: Salwa, you look as if you have a ghost.
quests.pitch: My husband Idrees was a ship's cook. His last ship was the Gilded Flagon, which went down off Suloon the winter before the Landing Light was rebuilt. They found no bodies. They found a flagon, once, on the beach, with its cork gone and nothing in it. I have kept it on the bar ever since. Last night it filled with seawater, by itself, and a line of letters swam to the surface. I am not a fanciful woman. Go and see.
quests.desc: The flagon on Salwa's bar filled with seawater by itself and showed letters. Her husband's ship, the Gilded Flagon, lies wrecked off the Landing.

objectives.text: Drive the drowned crew from the wreck of the Gilded Flagon
Search the galley of the Gilded Flagon
objectives.journal: In the galley, in a stew-pot nailed to the table, lay a waxed bundle. Inside was a letter in a ship's cook's round hand, never sent, and a wedding band that was a size too large for the wearer.

objectives.text: Bring the letter to Salwa of the Barnacle Bride
objectives.topic: It was in the galley, in the stew-pot. A letter, and your husband's ring.
objectives.reply: In the stew-pot. Of course. He kept everything there. "A good cook keeps what matters where the heat is." Let me read. ... Oh. Oh, the old fool. He says the ship was too slow, and the captain too proud, and that he did not mind. He says to tell me the stew was always meant for me. I think I need to sit.

quests.outro: The flagon on the bar of the Barnacle Bride stays dry. Salwa wears a wedding band on a cord, a little too large, and serves a stew that has, people say, a great deal of heart in it.

quests.title: The Island's Price
quests.offer: Salim, what is the price of this map?
quests.pitch: Half a map. It shows the hidden dock of Stros M'Kai, the one the Toll-Reeve does not tax and the Captain does not admit exists. I had it from a dying man, who had it from another. The other half is held by Captain Makki, who will not sell it, because it shows the dock too. Two halves make a whole, and a whole makes a very large problem for someone. Take my half. Pay the toll. Find the dock. Steal the other, or defend it.
quests.desc: Old Salim sells half of the map to Stros M'Kai's hidden dock. The other half is held by Captain Makki. A toll, a hidden dock and a choice of theft or defence await.

objectives.text: Take the half-map from Old Salim
objectives.topic: I will buy your half. What is the price?
objectives.reply: The price is that you do not ask where I got it. And that you pay the Toll-Reeve her due, so that she cannot say you were on the island without leave. A thief with a receipt is a customer. A thief without one is merely a thief.

objectives.text: Pay Toll-Reeve Zahra Vane the harbour toll in emeralds
objectives.topic: Five emeralds. The toll for one visitor, one satchel and one half-map.
objectives.reply: A half-map! You declared it. How very honest. The toll for a half-map is nothing, but the toll for the man who carries it is five. Thank you. A receipt, with my seal, and a word of advice: do not be seen near the north quay at night.

objectives.text: Wait for night and find the hidden dock beneath the harbour fort
Defeat Warden Hamza One-Eye, who guards the hidden dock
Face Captain Makki Red-Sail with both halves of the map
objectives.topic: I have both halves. The hidden dock is yours. What would you have me do with them?
objectives.reply: Both halves! In one pair of hands. Hm. The dock is the only thing between this island and a Crown garrison, and I would sooner it were mine than the Governor's. Give me the halves, and I will burn them. Or keep them, and sell the dock to the Governor, and watch what happens to a harbour that has no secret.

choices.label: Give him the map. A pirate's dock is a pirate's, and the island is more honest for it.
choices.reply: Then I will keep it, and I will keep it hidden. It is an old arrangement and a good one. Take a cut of the next ship in. I will make it a large one.

choices.label: Sell the dock to the Governor. A hidden harbour is a stolen harbour.
choices.reply: Then the Governor will have a garrison by spring, and a toll by summer, and a very large problem by autumn. I will say nothing to you. I will say a great deal to the sea.

quests.outro: The hidden dock of Stros M'Kai is known, or unknown, depending on whom you ask. Old Salim has sold a third map to a third man, and swears it is the first.

quests.title: The Lamp That Counts
quests.offer: Zahra, you want the lighthouse looked at?
quests.pitch: The Stros M'Kai light has been counting ships. Not shining: counting. Every ship that passes, it flashes once. Twice for a ship that does not pay. Someone has rigged the lamp to the toll-book, and I want to know who. I have my suspicions. I will not say whom. Go up. Look. Tell me if it is a man or a mechanism.
quests.desc: Stros M'Kai's lighthouse flashes once for every ship that passes and twice for those that do not pay the toll. Toll-Reeve Zahra Vane wants to know whether it is a man or a mechanism.

objectives.text: Clear the lighthouse base of whoever is guarding the rig
Climb to the lamp room and examine the toll-rig
objectives.journal: There was no mechanism. There was an old woman in a rocking chair, with a bell-rope in her hand and a long list of ships on her knee. She looked up and said, in the mildest way: "Oh, dear. Is it time for the next one? I do lose count."

objectives.text: Tell Toll-Reeve Vane who has been counting ships
objectives.topic: It is a woman, Reeve. An old woman with a bell-rope, who says she loses count. She has been doing it for years.
objectives.reply: An old woman! Gods. That is Auntie Nuri, who was the Governor's nurse when he was a child. I had forgotten she was alive. Hm. She is a better toll-collector than any I have hired. I will not stop her. I shall pay her. In sweets.

quests.outro: The lighthouse of Stros M'Kai still counts ships. Auntie Nuri sits in her rocking chair, and Toll-Reeve Vane brings her sweets each evening, and the toll-book has never been more accurate.

quests.title: The Tallest Tale in the Draggin' Tale
quests.offer: Brulla, you said nobody has won the free drink.
quests.pitch: My menu has forty stories, and I swear every one of them is true. The Kraken's Lunch, the Cursed Mudcrab, the Admiral's Wife. A drink is free only if your story is better than the one on the menu. I have been waiting years. I think the island has a better one than any of mine, but I cannot hear it, because I am always pouring. Ask around. Bring me the best. If it is better, I shall pour you a drink named after it.
quests.desc: Brulla of the Draggin' Tale will give a free drink to anyone who tells a better story than the forty on her menu. She wants you to gather the island's best.

objectives.text: Hear Captain Makki Red-Sail's tale
objectives.topic: Brulla says you have a tale better than anything on her menu. What is it?
objectives.reply: The Gull and the Governor. A seagull stole the Governor's wig on the morning of his coronation, and flew it to the roof of the harbour fort, and refused to give it back. The Governor stood in the square, bald, for a full hour, while the gull sat on the wig and ate his cake. I was there. I have never laughed so hard. I am the gull's patron to this day.

objectives.text: Hear Old Salim's tale
objectives.topic: Brulla says you have a tale better than anything on her menu. What is it?
objectives.reply: The Honest Map. A man sold a map of the island to three different buyers, each for a different treasure. All three followed it. All three dug in the same place. All three found each other. They set up a shop there. It is now the best-run chandlery on the north quay. The map was a lie. The shop is the truth. That is the best story I know.

objectives.text: Hear Toll-Reeve Zahra Vane's tale
objectives.topic: Brulla says you have a tale better than anything on her menu. What is it?
objectives.reply: The Toll That Was Paid Twice. A captain came in, paid his toll, and left. A day later he came back and paid again, for no reason. I asked why. He said the first time was for the harbour, and the second was for a debt he owed the previous reeve, who had saved his life and never asked for anything. He wanted to pay it. The old reeve was dead. So he paid it to me. I wept at my desk. It was the most honest toll I ever collected.

objectives.text: Tell Brulla which tale is the tallest
objectives.topic: I have three, Brulla. The gull and the Governor, the honest map, and the toll that was paid twice. Which one do you want?
objectives.reply: Three. And all three true. I shall have to decide, and I find that I want to hear them again. Tell me which you think is the best. I will put it on the menu in your name.

choices.label: The Gull and the Governor. It is the funniest.
choices.reply: Then it shall be The Gull's Wig, and the drink shall have a feather in it. I have never been so happy.

choices.label: The Honest Map. It is the cleverest.
choices.reply: The Honest Map. A sour drink with a little sweetness at the bottom. Yes. That is the island, and I love it.

choices.label: The Toll That Was Paid Twice. It is the truest.
choices.reply: Then I shall pour it plain, in a plain cup, and charge nothing. It is the only one I will not name. I know exactly who it is for.

quests.outro: The menu of the Draggin' Tale now has forty-one stories, and at least one of them is true. Brulla pours the drink in your name each time you visit and will not take payment.

quests.title: A Quiet Month on the Council
quests.pitch: The Cobalt Ledger went to the Crown Council. Vizier Samir ibn-Cassim has news.
quests.desc: The Cobalt Ledger went to the Crown Council. Vizier Samir ibn-Cassim has news.

objectives.text: Hear what the Crown Council made of the Cobalt Ledger
objectives.topic: The ledger is with the Council. What has changed?
objectives.reply: Four Crown lords have been asked to travel. Four Forebear factors have been asked to explain. Four others have been asked nothing at all, and those are the ones I watch. Sentinel is quiet, which is the sound a city makes when it is holding its breath. The palm-print in cobalt matches a hand I know. I will not say whose. Thank you. Take this, with the Council's regard.

quests.outro: The Crown Council has the Cobalt Ledger. Four lords have been asked to travel, and Sentinel holds its breath.

quests.title: The Factors Speak
quests.pitch: The Cobalt Ledger went to the Forebear speakers. Captain Layla Ashraf has a report from the docks.
quests.desc: The Cobalt Ledger went to the Forebear speakers. Captain Layla Ashraf has a report from the docks.

objectives.text: Hear Captain Ashraf's report from the docks after the Forebear reading
objectives.topic: The Forebears have the ledger. What do the docks say?
objectives.reply: Loud. The Forebear speakers read the names aloud from the Bazaar steps, in order, and three Crown lords left the city before the fourth. The Harbour Guild is in an uproar. The dye-sellers have doubled their prices. I have eleven men on the quay and a bad feeling in my sword-arm. But the cobalt is off the market, and nobody will be burned for it again. Take this.

quests.outro: The Forebears read the names of the Cobalt Ledger from the Bazaar steps. Sentinel is loud, and the cobalt is off the market.

quests.title: Ash in the Bazaar
quests.pitch: The Cobalt Ledger was burned. Zareen the Dye-Seller has noticed the smoke.
quests.desc: The Cobalt Ledger was burned. Zareen the Dye-Seller has noticed the smoke.

objectives.text: Hear what Zareen the Dye-Seller makes of the ashes
objectives.topic: The ledger is ash. Does the bazaar know?
objectives.reply: The whole bazaar knows. Not what was in it. That it burned. A smell like singed wool and old cobalt, over the awnings at dusk, and a very particular silence from the Harbour Guild. I have added a pinch of the ash to a new blue. It is a very beautiful colour. I call it Nothing Was Written. It sells like water in the desert.

quests.outro: A blue called Nothing Was Written sells in the Bazaar of Winds. The Cobalt Ledger is ash, and everyone knows it.

quests.title: The Ancestors' Light
quests.pitch: The beacon burns white. Stairs-Keeper Jul has been watching it.
quests.desc: The beacon burns white. Stairs-Keeper Jul has been watching it.

objectives.text: Sit with Stairs-Keeper Jul under the white beacon
objectives.topic: The beacon is white. What do you see?
objectives.reply: My grandmother, on the third landing, at dusk. She is not there. She is not a ghost. She is a place where the light is a little warmer. I did not tell the priests. I put the hundred-and-first step's lamp on her landing and I said her name. The white light is not for the town. It is for the stair. I have never been prouder of my count.

quests.outro: The white beacon of Elinhir lights the stair for those who climbed it before. Stairs-Keeper Jul counts a hundred and one, and says each name.

quests.title: Caravans by Gold Light
quests.pitch: The beacon burns gold and caravans are coming. Qadir Windfall has a full house.
quests.desc: The beacon burns gold and caravans are coming. Qadir Windfall has a full house.

objectives.text: Count the new custom at the Hundredth Step
objectives.topic: The beacon is gold. How is trade?
objectives.reply: Full. Every room on every landing, and a queue on the stair. Caravan masters, tax-men, a poet from Rihad who has paid for the top landing, which is mine, and which I have vacated, and which I regret. The raiders are fewer, because the watch is doubled. The wind sings a better song now, because it is drowned out by money. Have a drink. Have four.

quests.outro: The gold beacon of Elinhir draws caravans from the sand. The Hundredth Step has a queue on the stair, and Qadir Windfall has stopped sleeping.

quests.title: The Books Opened
quests.pitch: The arena's books are open and the fixed bout is public. Bookmaker Rim has a sour face.
quests.desc: The arena's books are open and the fixed bout is public. Bookmaker Rim has a sour face.

objectives.text: Visit Bookmaker Rim as the arena opens its books
objectives.topic: The books are open. How is business?
objectives.reply: Ruinous. The honest bettors are back, and the dishonest ones have gone, and I have discovered that I am best at neither. The Arena-Master has put my name on the notice board, in a very large hand. I am to give back eleven hundred. I shall, in instalments, and I shall make them very small. I will tell you this: a fair arena is a duller place. It is also a safer one for a man who owes you a favour.

quests.outro: The books of the Dragonstar arena are open and Bookmaker Rim pays his debts in small instalments. The seven fights are, at last, seven.

quests.title: The Star, Quietly
quests.pitch: You took the star without opening the arena's books. Gladiator Safiya has thoughts.
quests.desc: You took the star without opening the arena's books. Gladiator Safiya has thoughts.

objectives.text: Hear Safiya's thoughts on the quiet victory
objectives.topic: I took the star quietly. What do you make of it?
objectives.reply: It is a pretty thing. I held it for a night, once, and I put it back, because I did not trust my own hands. You have taken it and left the arena standing. I do not know if you were wise or cowardly. I will say that Dahab has sacked Odalric's partner, and that Rim now takes only honest bets, mostly, and that I have not been paid this quarter. I am content. It is the nearest I have come to happiness in a pit.

quests.outro: The Star of Dragonstar bears a new name, and the arena's books are closed. The seven fights are honest, mostly, and nobody asks.

quests.title: The Dock Stays Dark
quests.pitch: The hidden dock stays in Captain Makki's keeping. He promised you a cut of the next ship in.
quests.desc: The hidden dock stays in Captain Makki's keeping. He promised you a cut of the next ship in.

objectives.text: Collect your cut from Captain Makki Red-Sail
objectives.topic: The dock is yours. Where is my cut?
objectives.reply: In the hold of a brig called the Evening Gull, which came in last night. I did not ask what she carried. I never do. There is a share under the third crate, marked with a gull. Take it, and a bit extra for the trouble. The Governor has asked twice about the dock. I told him it was a rumour. He said he would see. I said, "See what?" It is a very good answer.

quests.outro: The hidden dock of Stros M'Kai stays hidden. Captain Makki Red-Sail pays his debts in brig-loads and keeps his counsel in the dark.

quests.title: A Garrison by Spring
quests.pitch: The Governor now holds the map of the hidden dock. Toll-Reeve Zahra Vane has seen the garrison arrive.
quests.desc: The Governor now holds the map of the hidden dock. Toll-Reeve Zahra Vane has seen the garrison arrive.

objectives.text: Hear Toll-Reeve Vane's account of the garrison's arrival
objectives.topic: The Governor has the dock. What has changed?
objectives.reply: Fifty men by spring, and a toll-house on the north quay. The harbour is quieter, and the Draggin' Tale has half the custom, and Captain Makki sits on his deck with his chin on his fist. I record the new tolls. They are recorded in the Governor's favour. I find I do not like it. I find I never liked the old ones, either. I am a toll-reeve. We are not made to like things.

quests.outro: A garrison stands on the north quay of Stros M'Kai, and the hidden dock is a toll-house. Captain Makki sits on his deck, and the sea is the same.
